x: Two members of the club, Bert Clayton and Jack Stirling-Wakeley, took part in this year's Nijmegen Marches and we produce some extracts from an article by Bert Clayton published in an Eastleigh newspaper.

We were saddened to learn at a recent Committee meeting that Jack Stirling-Wakeley died suddenly last December from Coronary Thrombosis. Always interested in amateur sport, Jack developed an interest in long-distance walking when serving in the Middle East during the 1939-1945 war.

1948 saw a 24 hours race at Motspur Park which resulted in a Belgrave win for Jack Stirling-Wakeley, whose death was recently reported. He covered 100 miles in 18:56:13 to become No. 143 and went on to cover 122 miles 1411 yards.
This was first produced in December 1952 by one of our walkers, Jack Stirling-Wakeley (winner of 24 Hours Track Walk at Motspur Park in 1948 and the London to Brighton and Back Walk in 1951).
Stan Vicker's 1 hour mark was 8mls.702yds., Ray Middleton's 6, 7 and 8 hour marks were 40mls.581yds., 46mls.1264yds. and 53mls.352yds., Jack Stirling-Wakeley's 24 hours mark was 122mls.1411yds.
